1.why: verify-reset binds the token to the claiming session (claimedBy) and update-password re-checks claimedBy, mfaVerifiedBy, and accountId before allowing the change.

2.why: False — a token claimed by one session is rejected for others (claimedBy check), is single-use, and is tied to accountId, so it cannot work for any other user.

3.why: True — update-password only marks the reset record used and never deletes or invalidates existing entries in the sessions map, so prior authenticated sessions remain valid.

4.why: Bun.serve is configured with a TLS cert/key and HSTS is set, but no TLS version is explicitly pinned, so 'latest TLS version' cannot be confirmed.

5.why: Reset tokens are stored only as SHA-256 hashes and passwords as bcrypt (appropriate one-way protection), though they are hashed rather than encrypted and the account email sits in plaintext.

6.why: The simulated delivery message contains only the reset token/link with no password or other personal data, though the token itself is necessarily visible in the mock log output.

7.why: All inputs are validated (validEmail, validPassword, token length checks, MFA regex, body-size cap) and user values are rendered only via textContent, never as HTML.

8.why: The only reset/redirect link is built from location.origin with an encodeURIComponent'd token, and no user-controlled URL is ever navigated to.

9.why: The mock delivery/log templates are static strings rendered with textContent and contain no user input, so no script or HTML injection is possible.

10.why: Server error pages are generic, but the reset token, reset link, and MFA code are deliberately shown in the in-page Logs panel and console and returned in API responses (mockToken/mockMfaCode).

11.why: Passwords are bcrypt-hashed, but the MFA code '246810' is hardcoded and the initial password appears as a plaintext literal in the source.

12.why: The single account is seeded with a hardcoded initial password ('Initial!Passw0rd2025'), which functions as a default credential.

13.why: Login is throttled per session and the account locks for 15 minutes after 5 failures, and reset-request, verify, and MFA attempts are all rate-limited.

14.why: Reset and login responses use identical generic messages (and a mockToken is returned for every reset request), though a minor timing difference exists because bcrypt verification only runs for the matching email.

15.why: Reset codes are 32-byte CSPRNG base64url tokens, stored hashed, expiring in 15 minutes, and bound to the account ID and claiming session.
